title: Austin Energy's Environmental & Budget Focus
summary:
*   **Green Energy Discussion:** Officials held a public discussion on environmental policy issues directly impacting Austin Energy, the city's electric utility.
*   **Power Company Operations:** A briefing was provided on Austin Energy's General Manager's report, offering insights into the utility's performance and operations.
*   **City Budget Outlook:** A presentation detailed the overall financial health and future projections for the city's main operating fund.
transcript:
CITY COUNCIL WORKSESSION 
JANUARY 15, 2003
Austin City Council
MINUTES
WORKSESSION
WEDNESDAY, JANUARY 15,2003
The following represents the actions taken by the Austin City Council in the order they occurred
during the meeting.
The City Council of Austin, Texas convened in a Work Session on Wednesday, January 15, 2003 at
One Texas Center, 505 Barton Springs Road, 3rd Floor Training Room, Austin, Texas.
Mayor Garcia called the meeting to order at 10:01 a.m.
Mayor Garcia recessed the Work Session at 10:02 a.m. to go into the Executive Session.
EXECUTIVE SESSION
Public Power Utility Competitive Matters-Section 551.086
1. 
Discuss competitive strategies and financial planning issues for Austin Energy.
Executive Session ended at 11:00 a.m.
Mayor Garcia called the Worksession back to order at 11:02 a.m.
Briefings
2. 
Presentation of Austin Energy's General Manager's Report and discussion of
environmental policy issues.
The presentation was made by Toby Hammett Futrell, City Manager, and Juan Garza,
General Manager, and Roger Duncan, Vice President, Austin Energy.
3. 
Briefing on the financial outlook of the General Fund (Budget Office).
The presentation was made by Toby Hammett Futrell, City Manager, and Rudy Garza,
Budget Officer.
The motion to adjourn the meeting at 12:08 p.m. was approved on Council Member Wynii's motion,
Council Member Dimkerley's second on a 7-0 vote.
The minutes for the Work Session of January 15, 2003 were approved on January 30, 2003 on
Council Member Thomas' motion, Council Member Dimkerley's second on a 7-0 vote.
